flags.headline: Wildfire-reform deadline is tomorrow (Aug 31); weekend reporting shows lawmakers rejecting key parts of Newsom's utility-liability relief package
flags.detail: No new price data since Friday's close ($70.14, -4.80%) -- markets are closed through the weekend. But the qualitative picture escalated: CalMatters reported over the weekend that, with the legislative session ending Aug 31, Assembly and Senate lawmakers are balking at several of Gov. Newsom's core proposals -- including limits on wildfire-survivor pain-and-suffering damages and curbs on insurer reimbursement claims -- that were meant to give utilities like Edison financial relief. Newsom is making a last-minute push, but as of this run no compromise bill has passed. This is now a one-day-out binary event for the session: either a reform bill lands by tomorrow's deadline or it doesn't, directly bearing on CEO Pedro Pizarro's public credit-downgrade warning.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'California's inverse condemnation doctrine holds utilities liable for wildfire damages regardless of negligence, creating a unique and structurally uninsurable business model risk' and the D/E 216% financial-cushion risk. A failed or watered-down reform bill at tomorrow's deadline would be this risk materializing, not just a standing structural concern. Persisting RED, escalated urgency (deadline moved from 3 days out to 1 day out; lawmaker pushback is new since Friday).
